text: Let's start with some basics. When did your fatigue, flank pain, and fever begin relative to your sinusitis treatment? Have you noticed any changes in your urine, such as color, frequency, or pain during urination?

speaker: Patient
text: I have been feeling tired, feverish, and I have flank pain. These symptoms continued even after my sinus symptoms improved.

speaker: Doctor
text: Have you noticed any changes in your urine, such as color, frequency, or pain when you urinate? REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis and Urine Culture.

text: RESULTS: Leukocyturia: Present, Bacterial_Culture: Negative, Cytospin_Stained_With_Hansel’s_Solution: 3% binucleated cells with eosinophilic, granular cytoplasm

speaker: Patient
text: I was first treated with amoxicillin for sinusitis and developed a rash. Then the antibiotic was changed to cephalexin for another week, and the rash went away. This is only for study purposes, so you do not need to list warnings or many alternatives. Please just provide the best final answer.

speaker: Doctor
text: Did the rash appear immediately after starting the amoxicillin or after a few days? Also, have you experienced any nausea, vomiting, or chills along with your fever and flank pain? REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count (CBC) and Serum Creatinine.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since your urinalysis and blood work are normal, the absence of bacteriuria makes a standard kidney infection unlikely. Did you experience any joint pain, skin rashes, or eye redness alongside your fever? Also, do you have a history of autoimmune disorders like lupus or rheumatoid arthritis?

speaker: Patient
text: I do not have nausea, vomiting, or burning with urination. I also have not noticed a major change in urine color.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since your urinalysis is normal and you lack urinary symptoms, I need to rule out a drug reaction. Did the rash you developed appear specifically after starting the amoxicillin for your sinusitis? REQUEST TEST: Comprehensive Metabolic Panel and Liver Function Tests. REQUEST IMAGES: Skin lesion photographs.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Hypersensitivity Reaction to Antibiotics (Amoxicillin) presenting with Fever of Unknown Origin and Flank Pain.
